1.word_for_word: ṣaṣṭhe — in the sixth chapter; sakhyuḥ girā — because of his friend’s words; nandaḥ vrajam gacchan — Nanda, going back to Vraja; mṛtām rākṣasīm pathi dṛṣṭvā — seeing the dead Rākṣasī on the way; tasyāḥ mṛtyum śrutvā — hearing of her death; atha vismitaḥ — then becoming astonished.
1.translation: In the sixth chapter Nanda, returning to Vraja because of his friend’s warning, sees the dead Rākṣasī and, after hearing how she died, becomes astonished.

3.word_for_word: kṛṣṇa-viṣaye śaṅkamānam rājānam prati — addressing the king who is anxious about Kṛṣṇa; aviṣaye pravṛttā sā eva mariṣyati — the demoness, acting where she has no proper sphere, will herself die; yatra śrī-kṛṣṇasya śravaṇa-ādīni na santi — where hearing and the other devotional practices concerning Śrī Kṛṣṇa are absent; tatra eva tāsām śaktiḥ — only there do such beings have power; sākṣāt tasmin eva sati — when Kṛṣṇa Himself is directly present; kā śaṅkā — what cause is there for anxiety?
3.translation: To reassure the king, who is anxious about Kṛṣṇa, Śrīdhara indicates that Pūtanā, entering a place where her power has no proper scope, will herself die. Beings such as her have power only where hearing and the other devotional practices concerning Śrī Kṛṣṇa are absent. When Kṛṣṇa Himself is directly present, what cause for anxiety can there be?

4.word_for_word: yoṣitvā — having taken the appearance of a woman; veṣataḥ varām nārīm iva ātmānam vidhāya — fashioning herself in dress and appearance like an excellent woman; nirlajjā nirviśaṅkā ca satī — being shameless and without fear; katham para-sadmani praviṣṭā — how could she enter another person’s house?; kāma-cāriṇī — one who moves wherever she wishes; na hi kāma-cāriṇīṣu idam citram — such conduct is not surprising in one who roams at will.
4.translation: ‘Yoṣitvā’ means that Pūtanā fashioned herself in appearance like an excellent woman. If one asks how, shameless and fearless, she could simply enter another person’s house, the answer is ‘kāma-cāriṇī’: for one who goes wherever she wishes, such behavior is not surprising.

5-6.word_for_word: valgu-smita-apāṅga-visarga-vīkṣitaiḥ — by glances whose sidelong movements were accompanied by a charming smile; vraja-okasām manaḥ harantīm — stealing the minds of the people of Vraja; gopāḥ hṛta-manastvena — the cowherd men, their minds captivated; tām na nivāritavantaḥ — did not prevent her; gopyaḥ ca śriyam iva matvā — and the gopīs, thinking her to be like Śrī, Lakṣmī; tūṣṇīm āsan — remained silent; kena api anivāritā — stopped by no one; praviveśa — she entered.
5-6.translation: By her glances, whose sidelong movements were accompanied by a charming smile, she stole the minds of the people of Vraja. The cowherd men, their minds captivated, did not stop her, and the gopīs, thinking her to be like Lakṣmī herself, remained silent. Thus no one prevented her from entering.

8.word_for_word: carācara-ātmatvāt eva — because He is the Self of all moving and unmoving beings; tām vibudhya — recognizing her; nimīlita-īkṣaṇaḥ āsa — He remained with His eyes closed; svayam anantam — the infinite Lord Himself; duṣṭānām antakam — the destroyer of the wicked; bālam matvā — taking Him to be an ordinary child; sā aṅkam āropayat — she placed Him on her lap; yathā uragam suptam — like a sleeping serpent; abuddhiḥ rajju-dhīḥ — an ignorant person thinking it a rope; ajñānataḥ rajju-buddhyā gṛhṇāti — grasping it through the mistaken idea that it is a rope; tadvat — so Pūtanā acted.
8.translation: Because He is the Self of all moving and unmoving beings, Kṛṣṇa recognized Pūtanā and closed His eyes. She, however, took the infinite Lord—the destroyer of the wicked—for an ordinary child and placed Him on her lap, like an ignorant person who mistakes a sleeping serpent for a rope and grasps it.

9.word_for_word: nanu yaśodā-rohiṇyau tām katham na nyavārayetām — why did Yaśodā and Rohiṇī not stop her?; vāmam — charming, lovely; jananyā iva ceṣṭitam — conduct like that of a mother; vara-striyam — an excellent woman; sahasā eva antarā gṛha-madhye vīkṣya — suddenly seeing her inside the house; antaḥ taikṣṇye bahir mārdave — inwardly sharp and outwardly soft; kośa-paricchada-asi-vat — like a sword enclosed in a soft decorative sheath; tat-prabhayā dharṣite — overwhelmed by her splendor; aham asya jananī iyam vā iti mohite — bewildered as though wondering ‘Am I His mother, or is she?’; kevalam nirīkṣamāṇe atiṣṭhatām — the two mothers merely stood watching; na tu nivāritavatyau — they did not restrain her.
9.translation: If one asks why Yaśodā and Rohiṇī did not stop her, the verse answers that they suddenly saw an excellent woman whose conduct was charming and motherlike. Her inner cruelty concealed beneath outward softness was like a sharp sword within a soft, decorated sheath. Overpowered by her splendor and bewildered—as though wondering, ‘Am I His mother, or is she?’—the two mothers merely stood watching and did not restrain her.

10.word_for_word: tasmin sthāne — there; durjaram vīryam viṣam yasmin — whose potency, the poison, was unbearable; tam stanam — that breast; śrī-kṛṣṇam aṅkam ādāya — taking Śrī Kṛṣṇa on her lap; tasmai śiśave dadau — she gave it to the child; atha anantaram eva — immediately afterward; prapīḍya — pressing it firmly; kevalam viṣam apathyam iti matvā iva — as though regarding the poison as wholly unwholesome; tasyāḥ prāṇaiḥ saha apibat — He drank it together with her life-air.
10.translation: Pūtanā took Kṛṣṇa on her lap and offered Him the breast containing its unbearable potency, the poison. Immediately Kṛṣṇa pressed it firmly and, as though regarding the poison itself as something unwholesome to be removed, drank it together with her life-air.

12.word_for_word: rasāḥ — the rasas; rasā-talāni ca — also the subterranean Rasātala regions.
12.translation: ‘Rasāḥ’ also includes the subterranean Rasātala regions, which echoed with her terrible cry.

13.word_for_word: vyādāya — opening wide; mukham vivṛtya — opening her mouth; nija-rūpam āsthitā — assuming her own form; maraṇa-samaye — at the time of death; kapaṭam ayuktam iti iva — as though deception were no longer appropriate.
13.translation: ‘Vyādāya’ means opening her mouth wide. At death Pūtanā resumed her own form, as though deception were no longer fitting at the moment of death.

14.word_for_word: patann api — even while falling; tasyāḥ dehaḥ — her body; paṭa-kośa-madhya-vartinaḥ drumān — the trees standing within the surrounding tract; cūrṇī-cakāra — crushed to pieces.
14.translation: Even as Pūtanā’s enormous body fell, it crushed the trees standing within the surrounding tract.

15-17.word_for_word: īṣā-mātra-ugra-daṁṣṭra-āsyam — a mouth whose terrible teeth were as large as a plough beam; girikandara-vat nāsike — nostrils like mountain caves; gireḥ cyutau sthūla-upalau iva stanau — breasts like huge boulders fallen from a mountain; raudram — terrifying; prakīrṇā aruṇā mūrdha-jāḥ — scattered reddish hair; andha-kūpau iva gabhīre akṣiṇī — eyes deep like dark wells; pulina-vat ārohau jaghane — broad hips like sandy riverbanks; baddhāḥ setavaḥ iva bhujau ūrū aṅghrī ca — arms, thighs and feet like massive embankments; śūnya-toya-hrada iva udaram — a belly like a reservoir emptied of water; kalevaram vīkṣya — seeing that corpse; gopāḥ gopyaḥ ca santrastuḥ — the cowherd men and women were terrified; pūrvam eva tasyāḥ śabdena bhītāḥ — already frightened by her sound; punaḥ darśanena ati-trasuḥ — they were even more terrified by seeing her.
15-17.translation: The cowherd men and women were terrified on seeing Pūtanā’s corpse. Śrīdhara unpacks the verse’s comparisons: her mouth bore terrible teeth as large as a plough beam; her nostrils were like mountain caves; her breasts like massive boulders fallen from a mountain; her reddish hair was scattered wildly; her eyes were deep like dark wells; her broad hips resembled sandy riverbanks; her arms, thighs and feet were like great embankments; and her belly was like an empty reservoir. They had already been shaken by the terrible sound of her fall, and the sight of the body frightened them still more.

20.word_for_word: dvādaśa-aṅgeṣu — on the twelve bodily parts; lalāṭa-ādiṣu — beginning with the forehead; keśava-ādi-dvādaśa-nāmabhiḥ — with the twelve divine names beginning with Keśava.
20.translation: On the twelve bodily parts beginning with the forehead, they performed protection with the twelve names of the Lord beginning with Keśava.

21.word_for_word: anāchāntāḥ eva — before even performing ācamana; prathamam ati-sambhrameṇa — at first, because of extreme alarm; rakṣām kṛtvā — having performed protection; kiñcit labdha-śvāsāḥ — after recovering some composure; punaḥ tātparyeṇa bīja-nyāsam akurvata — they then deliberately performed seed-syllable placement; saṁspṛṣṭa-salilāḥ — having touched or sipped purifying water; āchāntāḥ — having performed ācamana; ātmani prathamam — first upon themselves; aṅgeṣu karayoḥ ca pṛthak — separately upon the limbs and hands; ajādi-ekādaśa-bījānām madhye — among the eleven seed syllables beginning with ‘a’; kara-śuddhau trīṇi — three for hand purification; karayoḥ sandhiṣu catvāri catvāri — four at the joints of each hand; aṅghry-ādau ekasmin aṅge ekam ekam bījam — one seed on each bodily part beginning with the feet; bālasya api aṅgeṣu tathā eva — and then the same upon the child’s limbs.
21.translation: At first, in their panic, the gopīs performed protective rites without even doing ācamana. When they recovered some composure, they deliberately performed bīja-nyāsa. ‘Saṁspṛṣṭa-salilāḥ’ means that they had taken purifying water. They first placed the prescribed seed syllables on their own hands and limbs—three for hand purification, four at the joints of each hand, and one on each bodily part beginning with the feet—and then performed the same placement on the child.

22-23.word_for_word: diśu rakṣām akurvan — they performed protection in the directions; cakra-sahitaḥ hariḥ tava agrataḥ astu — may Hari with the discus stand before you; saha-gadaḥ hariḥ tava paścāt astu — may Hari with the mace stand behind you; tvat-pārśvayoḥ dhanur-dharaḥ madhuhā asi-dharaḥ ca āstām — may the bow-bearer and Madhuhā bearing the sword stand at your two sides; śaṅkha-dharaḥ urugāyaḥ catuḥ-koṇeṣu — may Urugāya bearing the conch guard the four corners; upari upendraḥ — Upendra above; kṣitau adhastāt — protection below upon the earth; haladharaḥ puruṣaḥ samantāt — Haladhara and Puruṣa all around.
22-23.translation: They next established protection in every direction: may Hari bearing the discus stand before the child and Hari with the mace behind; may the bow-bearer and Madhuhā with the sword guard the two sides; may Urugāya with the conch guard the corners; may Upendra protect above, protection be established below upon the earth, and Haladhara and Puruṣa guard all around.

24.word_for_word: evam bahiḥ rakṣām kṛtvā — having thus established external protection; antaraṅgām akurvan — they established inward protection; indriyāṇi iti — beginning with the verse about the senses.
24.translation: Having established protection externally in every direction, the gopīs now established inward protection, beginning with the senses.

25-26.word_for_word: ātmānam — the self; ahaṅkāram — here glossed as the ego, the sense of self-identification.
25-26.translation: Within this protective sequence Śrīdhara glosses ‘ātmānam’ as ahaṅkāra, the principle of ego or self-identification.

27-29.word_for_word: ātmānam — the self; ahaṅkāram — the ego, the sense of self-identification; the same brief Śrīdhara gloss belongs to the larger protection passage extending through these verses.
27-29.translation: In this continuing protective passage, Śrīdhara’s brief gloss identifies ‘ātmānam’ with ahaṅkāra, the ego or sense of self-identification.

30.word_for_word: sannyaveśayat — she laid Him down; chādayām āsa — she covered Him.
30.translation: ‘Sannyaveśayat’ means that Yaśodā laid the child down and covered Him.

32.word_for_word: vismayam eva āha — the verse expresses their astonishment; nūnam iti — with the word ‘surely’; bata — an exclamation of wonder; sāmpratam saḥ ṛṣiḥ — perhaps he has now become a seer; tapaḥ-prabhāvavān — powerful through austerity; yogeśaḥ — a master of yoga; jñānī vā — or a knower; samyak āsa — he must truly have become so; yataḥ saḥ eva dṛṣṭaḥ — because the very danger he had foretold was actually seen.
32.translation: The verse expresses the cowherds’ astonishment. ‘Bata’ is an exclamation of wonder. They reasoned that Vasudeva must truly be a seer empowered by austerity, a master of yoga, or a man of extraordinary knowledge, since the very danger he had foretold had now actually appeared.

34.word_for_word: vismaya-antaram āha — another marvel is described; kṛṣṇena nirbhuktaḥ — she had been sucked by Kṛṣṇa; ataḥ eva — precisely because of this; sapadi āhataḥ pāpmā yasya — her sin was immediately destroyed; dahyamānasya dehasya dhūmaḥ — the smoke of her burning body; aguru-saurabhaḥ — possessed the fragrance of aguru.
34.translation: Another marvel is described: because Kṛṣṇa had sucked from Pūtanā’s breast, her sin was immediately destroyed. Consequently the smoke rising from her burning body carried the fragrance of aguru.

35-36.word_for_word: prasaṅgāt — in connection with this event; kaimutya-nyāyena — by the a-fortiori principle, ‘how much more’; bhakti-vaibhavam āha — he shows the greatness of devotion; śraddhayā — with faith; āstikyena — with genuine conviction; bhaktyā — with devotion; premṇā — with love; raktāḥ — attached, affectionate; snigdhāḥ — tenderly loving; tan-mātaraḥ — ‘His mothers,’ plural; vatsāharaṇa-līlā-abhiprāyeṇa — with reference to the later calf-stealing pastime; go-gopikāḥ tadā mātaraḥ abhavan — when the cows and gopīs also became His mothers.
35-36.translation: Śrīdhara uses an a-fortiori argument to show the greatness of devotion. ‘Śraddhayā’ means with genuine faith; ‘bhaktyā,’ with love; and ‘raktāḥ,’ tenderly attached. The plural ‘His mothers’ anticipates the calf-stealing pastime, when the cows and gopīs also became Kṛṣṇa’s mothers. If Pūtanā attained a blessed destination by offering her breast with murderous intent, how much more must those attain who lovingly offer their dearest possessions to Kṛṣṇa.

44.word_for_word: etat ārbhakam — this childhood deed; arbhaka-caritam — an exploit performed in infancy; kim tat — what deed?; pūtanā-mokṣam — the deliverance of Pūtanā.
44.translation: ‘Ārbhakam’ means this wondrous deed of Kṛṣṇa’s infancy. What deed is meant? The deliverance of Pūtanā.
